# How to file ITR-1 on the e-filing portal (salaried, one employer)

Last tested: [month year], desktop browser, Assessment Year 2026-27 (income earned 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026). Re-test the on-screen labels before you publish.

If you earn only a salary from one employer, you can file your ITR-1 yourself on the income tax e-filing portal in about 30 to 45 minutes, provided Form 16 is in hand. By the end you'll have a filed and e-verified return, with an acknowledgement number to prove it. This guide is for first-time filers with one salary, some bank interest and one house at most.

## Before you start

- Form 16 (Part A and Part B) from your employer.
- Your PAN, linked to Aadhaar and showing as operative. The portal won't let a return through otherwise.
- Your e-filing login: your PAN is the user ID. If you haven't registered on incometax.gov.in, do that first.
- Your Annual Information Statement (AIS) and Form 26AS, downloaded from the portal. Bank interest often shows up here before you remember it.
- A bank account number and IFSC for your refund, and net banking or an Aadhaar-linked mobile for e-verification.
- ITR-1 is only for total income up to Rs 50 lakh from salary, one house property and other sources such as interest. If you sold shares or have a business, you need a different form.

## Steps

1. Open incometax.gov.in and click "Login". Enter your PAN as User ID and click "Continue".
2. Tick the secure access message, enter your password and click "Continue". If the portal asks for an OTP, enter it.
3. On the dashboard, click "e-File", then "Income Tax Returns", then "File Income Tax Return".
4. Select Assessment Year "2026-27" and click "Continue".
   [Screenshot alt text: the "File Income Tax Return" page with the Assessment Year drop-down set to 2026-27.]
5. Choose Mode of Filing "Online", then Status "Individual", and click "Continue".
6. Select "ITR-1", pick the reason that matches you (for most salaried people, taxable income above the basic exemption limit), and click "Let's Get Started".
7. Open "Personal Information". Check name, address, mobile and email. Under bank details, confirm the account where you want the refund. Mark it as the refund account.
8. Open "Gross Total Income". Compare the pre-filled salary with Part B of your Form 16. Under "Income from Other Sources", add interest from savings accounts and FDs. Use the AIS figure.
   [Screenshot alt text: the Gross Total Income section showing salary and interest rows with the pre-filled amounts.]
9. Choose your tax regime. The new regime applies by default; opt out of it only if your deductions (80C, 80D, home loan interest) make the old regime cheaper. Then open "Total Deductions" and enter only what you have proof for.
10. Open "Tax Paid" and check that the TDS on your Form 16 matches Form 26AS. Then open "Total Tax Liability" to see tax payable or refund.
11. If tax is payable, click "Pay Now" and pay by net banking or UPI, then return to the form. If not, click "Preview", read every section, then click "Proceed to Validation" and "Proceed to Verification".
   [Screenshot alt text: the Preview page of the return with the tax computation open.]
12. Under "e-Verify", choose "Aadhaar OTP" (or net banking), enter the OTP and click "Validate". You have 30 days after filing to e-verify.

## Check it worked

You'll see a success screen with a Transaction ID and an Acknowledgement Number. Save both. You'll also get an email and an SMS from the department. To confirm later, go to "e-File", "Income Tax Returns", "View Filed Returns" and check that your return for 2026-27 shows as e-verified. Refunds come after the department processes the return, to the account you marked in step 7.

## Common problems and fixes

**Login fails because your PAN is inoperative.** Cause: PAN isn't linked to Aadhaar. Fix: link it on the portal under "Link Aadhaar", pay the fee if asked, wait for the status to turn operative, then log in again.

**Salary on screen doesn't match Form 16.** Cause: your employer filed TDS data late or with an error. Fix: file using Form 16 Part B and ask HR to correct their TDS return. A mismatch left alone can bring a notice.

**Refund account shows as not validated.** Cause: the bank account was never pre-validated. Fix: go to "Profile", "My Bank Account", add the account and validate it, then come back to step 7. A refund can't be credited to an unvalidated account.

**OTP doesn't arrive for e-verification.** Cause: your Aadhaar-linked mobile number isn't the one you use. Fix: e-verify through net banking, or use a pre-validated bank account's EVC. Don't leave it for day 30.

## What next, and quick answers

Stuck, or unsure about the regime or a mismatch? Book [Firm name]'s Rs 999 assisted filing and a CA from our team will file it with you: [booking link].

**Can I file from my phone?** Yes, the portal works in a mobile browser, but the menus collapse. A laptop is easier for step 9.

**What if the due date has passed?** You can still file a belated return, with a late fee under section 234F of Rs 5,000, or Rs 1,000 if your total income is up to Rs 5 lakh. [Confirm the current due date before publishing.]

**I found a mistake after filing.** File a revised return for the same year. Don't file a second original.

# What is a credit score, and what moves it in India?

A credit score is a 3-digit number between 300 and 900 that a credit bureau calculates from your borrowing and repayment record. Lenders use it to guess how likely you are to repay. In India, four bureaus licensed by the RBI hold these records: TransUnion CIBIL, Experian, Equifax and CRIF High Mark. A higher score usually means easier approvals and better terms.

## Why does a credit score matter for your first credit card?

If you have never borrowed, a bank has nothing to judge you on. No record is not the same as a good record. Applicants with no history are often declined, or offered a small limit, and each application you make leaves a mark on your report.

So the first year decides a lot. A modest first limit, handled well, tends to be raised later; the same card handled badly can follow you into your first home loan. Your salary slip tells a lender what you earn. Your score tells it how you behave with money you owe.

## How does a credit score actually work?

Think of it as a batting average. One big innings does not fix a string of ducks. The bureau looks at the whole record, and these five things carry the weight:

- **Payment history.** Did you pay every EMI and card bill on time? This is the most important factor. Bureaus do not publish exact weights.
- **Credit utilisation.** How much of your card limit you use. Using Rs 25,000 of a Rs 1,00,000 limit is 25%. Bureaus advise keeping this low, commonly under 30%.
- **Length of history.** How long your oldest account has been open.
- **Mix of credit.** A card plus an instalment loan looks steadier than one card alone.
- **New enquiries.** Each time a lender checks your report for a fresh application, it records a hard enquiry.

Your income is not on this list. Bureaus do not see it.

### A worked example: Aarav and Meera

Both are 24, both earn well, and both got a card with a Rs 1,00,000 limit twelve months ago. These numbers are illustrative, not real customers.

| | Aarav | Meera |
|---|---|---|
| Monthly card spend | Rs 25,000 | Rs 70,000 |
| Utilisation | 25% | 70% |
| How the bill is paid | Full amount, before the due date | Minimum due, twice paid 10 days late |
| Applications in the last 3 months | 0 | 3 (a card and two loans) |

After a year, Aarav's report shows twelve on-time payments and a low balance. A lender sees steady behaviour. Meera's shows two late payments, a balance that never clears and three recent enquiries. A lender sees someone stretched. Aarav's limit is likely to be raised; Meera is likely to be declined for the next card, even though she earns the same.

Late payments can stay visible on a report for years. A low balance can be rebuilt in a few months.

## Credit score, credit report, enquiry: what is the difference?

| Term | What it is |
|---|---|
| Credit report | The full record: every loan and card, balances, payment status month by month. |
| Credit score | One number summarising that report. |
| Hard enquiry | A lender checks your report because you applied for credit. It is recorded. |
| Soft enquiry | You check your own score, or a lender pre-screens you. It does not hurt your score. |

Also, "CIBIL score" is one bureau's score, not the only one. The four bureaus hold slightly different data and use their own models, so your numbers can differ a little.

## What are the common credit score myths?

**Myth: checking my own score lowers it.** It does not. A self-check is a soft enquiry. Only a lender's hard enquiry for a new application counts. [Source: TransUnion CIBIL consumer FAQ, link, date.]

**Myth: a higher salary gives a higher score.** The bureau record has no income field. Salary helps you get a larger limit, not a better score. [Source: bureau FAQ, link, date.]

**Myth: carrying a balance builds your score.** You do not need to. Paying the full bill on time builds the same record, and you avoid the interest. [Source: bureau FAQ, link, date.]

**Myth: closing an old card helps.** It can hurt. You lose its history and its limit, and your utilisation on the remaining cards goes up. [Source: bureau FAQ, link, date.]

## What should you do next?

First, find your starting point.

- **No score yet:** Open one card or a small loan, use it lightly and pay in full. Scores typically appear after about six months of reported activity. [Confirm with bureau FAQ, link, date.]
- **Under 650:** Fix payment history first. Pay everything on the due date and clear overdue amounts.
- **650 to 749:** Reduce utilisation and avoid new applications for a few months.
- **750 or above:** Many lenders treat this as good, but each lender sets its own cut-off. Apply for the card you want.

Do this before you apply, not after a rejection. Check your free score in the [App name] app: open [App name], go to "Credit score" and tap "Check my score". It takes about a minute, and it is a soft enquiry.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is a good credit score in India?** Many lenders treat 750 and above as good. Cut-offs vary by lender and by product, so a 720 can pass for one card and fail for another.

**How often does my score update?** Since 1 January 2025, the RBI requires banks and lenders to report to the bureaus every fortnight, not monthly. A repayment you make today can show within about two weeks. [Source: RBI circular, link, date.]

**Can I get a free credit report?** Yes. The RBI lets you request one free full credit report, with score, each calendar year from each credit information company. [Source: RBI circular, link, date.]

**Does paying the minimum due hurt my score?** It avoids a late mark, but the balance stays high and so does your utilisation, and you pay interest on what is left.

---

Sources: RBI circulars on the free annual credit report and fortnightly credit data reporting [links and dates to add]; TransUnion CIBIL, Experian, Equifax and CRIF High Mark consumer FAQ pages [links, date accessed].
Author: [name]. Reviewed by: [name and credential, e.g. certified credit counsellor]. Last updated: 6 October 2026.

samples.text:
# Hybrid work from 1 January 2027: your questions answered

Applies to: all employees and people managers, Hyderabad office
Owner: People team, [people@company email]
Last updated: 6 October 2026
Announcement: [link to the announcement email]
Items in [square brackets] need a People team decision before this goes live.

## The short version

- From 1 January 2027, we move from 5 office days a week to 3 office days and 2 home days.
- It applies to all 350 of us, managers included.
- Which 3 days: [People team: fixed company days, or chosen by each team].
- Your next step: read the answers for your group below. Managers, read both sections.

## For everyone

**What exactly changes on 1 January 2027?**
You come to the office 3 days a week instead of 5, and work from home the other 2. Working hours, your role, your team and your reporting line stay as they are.

**Which 3 days do I come in?**
[People team: state the days, e.g. "Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday for everyone", or "each team picks its days, approved by the department head by 1 December".] If your days are not confirmed by 1 December, write to the People team.

**Why are we doing this?**
[People team: one plain sentence with the real reason, not "flexibility and engagement".] It is a company decision and it starts on 1 January. We will review how it is working, and tell you the review date here: [date].

**Is this about cutting costs, or headcount?**
No. This decision is about where we work, not how many of us there are. [People team: confirm, and say plainly if office space or seating is also changing.] If anything about headcount ever changes, you will hear it from the leadership team directly, not from this page.

**Can I go fully remote?**
No, not under this policy. The standard for everyone is 3 days in the office. If a medical or family situation makes this hard, speak to your manager first, then write to the People team. We reply within [N] working days. [Confirm the exception route.]

**Will this affect my appraisal?**
No. Your appraisal looks at your goals and your results, not at how many days you spent at home. [People team to confirm.] Managers should judge the work, not the location.

**Will my salary or allowances change?**
Your fixed pay does not change because of this. [People team: state what happens to commute, internet or any home-working allowance, with the amount if it changes.]

**Is there a seat for me on office days?**
Yes. You book a seat through [tool] before you come. [People team: number of seats against 350 people, so staff can see that 3 days works.]

**Will my attendance be tracked?**
Yes, through [seat booking or access card data], so we know how many seats to keep. It is not used to rank people. [Confirm who sees this data and for what.]

**What if I miss an office day?**
If you are on leave, nothing more is needed. If you are working from home on an office day without approval, your manager will talk to you first. [Confirm any further steps.]

**My commute is long and 3 days a week is hard. What can I do?**
You can raise it, and we will listen, but the 3-day standard stays for now. Talk to your manager about which 3 days are easiest for you, since [days may be set by your team]. If the commute creates a real hardship, write to the People team with the details and we will look at it case by case. [Confirm.]

**Does this apply to people who join after 1 January?**
Yes. New joiners follow the 3-office, 2-home model from their first week, and their manager shares their office days in the first week. [People team: confirm for interns and contract staff.]

**Can I work from my hometown for a few weeks?**
Not by default. [People team: rule and approval route.] Ask your manager at least [N] days ahead.

**What happens on public holidays and on my leave days?**
They replace that day's work. You do not have to make up the office day. [Confirm.]

## For people managers

**How do I plan my team's office days?**
Agree the days with your team by [date]. Keep at least [N] days overlapping so everyone can meet in person. Share the plan with the People team.

**What if someone asks me for fully remote work?**
Do not agree or refuse on your own. Send them to the People team, and tell them when they can expect an answer. Promises made in a corridor create disputes later.

**What if someone does not follow the 3-day rule?**
Talk to them first and find out why. If it continues, tell the People team. Do not escalate on a first miss.

**How do I keep the 2 home days fair across my team?**
If some days are more popular, rotate them, and do not give the same people the quietest days every week. If one day is overloaded with meetings, move the meetings, not the people. Tell your team the plan in writing so nobody feels singled out.

**How do I run reviews and one-to-ones for a hybrid team?**
Keep your usual review cycle and fix one-to-ones in the calendar for the same time each week, in person or on a call. Judge outputs against goals, the same way for people in the office and at home.

**Where can I get help?**
Your HR business partner is the first call. [People team: manager briefing date and link.]

## Still have a question?

Write to [people@company email] or ask in [channel]. We answer within [N] working days. We will update this page on [date] and add new questions as they come in.

EDITOR'S NOTE (remove before publishing): the transcript notes were not available to the writer, so the answers are drafted for the founder's approval. Check every answer, figure and the two Hindi phrases against the transcript before release. Approval covers factual accuracy, not new wording.

"Buyers pay for the promise that it arrives": Jaipur founder [Name] on winning US boutique orders

[Name] is the founder of [Marketplace], a Jaipur marketplace that sells handicrafts from [number] artisan workshops to boutiques in the United States. She won her first US order [period] ago, and today [Marketplace] ships to [number] boutiques. For Indian SME exporters weighing the same market, her account of what US buyers asked for, where the early shipments went wrong and what is left of the margin is a practical one. She will speak at this newsletter's exporter webinar on [date]. This interview was edited for length and clarity.

**How did the first US boutique find you?**

I found her. I sent [number] samples to boutique owners whose shops I had seen on Instagram, with a one-page note on who made each piece and how long it takes. Most never replied. One owner in [US city] did, six weeks later, and asked for a larger order. I did not have a website worth showing her, so the one-page note did the work.

**What did she ask for first?**

Not price. She wanted photographs on a plain background, exact sizes in inches, wash instructions and a firm delivery date. In India we say "ho jayega" [it will get done], and that is a promise. There it is not an answer. She wanted a date she could put in her own email.

**Why the US, and not a nearer market?**

Boutique owners there pay for the story behind a piece, and they reorder. A buyer in [US city] who likes a table runner will come back for the napkins and the cushion covers. In my experience a nearer market haggles on the price of the first piece. A US boutique asks how long the second order will take.

**Why do boutiques buy through a marketplace and not direct from a workshop?**

One invoice, one shipment, one person to call. A boutique owner buying from [number] small workshops would handle [number] sets of paperwork, [number] bank transfers and [number] parcels arriving on different days. We take that on and check the goods before they leave. She pays us for the fact that the problem is now ours.

**How do you check an artisan's work before it ships?**

We inspect every piece for size, colour match and finish, and we photograph the batch in the same light as the listing. If a block-print has moved by a few millimetres, we tell the buyer before she finds out.

**What went wrong in the first year?**

Packaging, mostly. A shipment of [product type] arrived with [damage] because we packed for a domestic courier. We refunded the buyer, repacked [percentage]% of stock and changed the carton spec. Colour variance between batches was the second problem: two dyeing lots of the same indigo looked like two different products. We now photograph a master piece and match every lot to it. The lesson was that a buyer forgives a delay she was warned about, and does not forgive a surprise.

**How do you handle shipping and customs?**

We hold an Importer-Exporter Code and file the export paperwork ourselves. For small first orders we use courier, which costs more per kilo but is predictable. Larger orders go by [air or sea]. We quote the buyer a landed cost, so she is never surprised at the other end.

**How do you get paid, and when?**

For a new buyer, [X]% in advance and the balance before dispatch. We do not ship on credit to someone we have not worked with. Once a buyer has reordered [number] times, we move to [payment terms]. The advance also protects the artisans, because they are paid on our schedule, not on the buyer's.

**How do you price for a US boutique?**

We start from her shelf price and work backwards. She needs room to double the wholesale price, so we ask what she can sell the piece for and what the artisan needs to be paid. Then we see what shipping leaves. If the numbers do not work, we tell her, and sometimes we suggest a smaller piece or a different set rather than squeeze the price.

**Artisans say marketplaces squeeze them. What margin is left, and for whom?**

It is thin, and I will not pretend otherwise. On an average order, [Marketplace] keeps [X]% as commission, shipping and duty take [Y]%, and the artisan receives [Z]%. Our own margin after costs is [W]%. The artisan's share is higher than if they sold through a local trader, but I would rather say the number than hide it. If a buyer wants a discount, we cut our commission first, not the artisan's price.

**What would you tell an exporter starting this year?**

Start with one buyer and ten pieces. Send samples that look like the final product, not your best piece. Reply to every email within a day. Trust, our word is "bharosa", is built in small deliveries, not in a catalogue.

**What do you still do yourself?**

I still pack the first order of every new buyer myself. I put in a handwritten note about the person who made it. The discount is forgotten in a week. The note stays on the shelf.

[Name] is founder of [Marketplace], Jaipur. Find her at [LinkedIn or website]. To hear more, register for the exporter webinar: [link].

Content Marketing Manager (B2B SaaS)

Pune (Baner office), hybrid: 3 days a week in the office | Full time | 4 to 7 years' experience | Rs 18-26 lakh a year, fixed | Reports to the CMO

About the role
[Company] sells inventory software to pharma distributors. Our buyers are owners and operations heads at distributors, people who run on stock levels and thin margins, and they do not read generic marketing. We need a content marketing manager who can write for them: case studies, guides and articles that a distributor forwards to a partner. You will work with the CMO, our product team and our sales team, and you will own what we publish and why.

What you'll do
- Interview customers and our own product and sales teams, and turn those conversations into published pieces.
- Write long-form content: case studies, guides, white papers and blog articles.
- Plan a quarterly content calendar with the CMO, tied to pipeline, not word counts.
- Run SEO for the topics our buyers search, and update older pieces that lose traffic.
- Work with sales to find the questions prospects ask and answer them in print.
- Edit and brief freelance writers and a designer, and keep our quality bar.
- Report monthly on what content produced: visits, leads and demo requests.

What success looks like
- By month 3: you have spoken to at least 5 customers and published 2 pieces that came from those conversations. A two-quarter content plan is agreed with the CMO.
- By month 6: 4 customer case studies are live, and one guide is generating leads we can trace in [CRM].
- By month 12: content is a reported source of demo requests every month. You and the CMO set the target in month 3.

Must-haves
- 4 to 7 years of B2B content marketing experience, ideally for software or another complex product.
- Published long-form work you wrote yourself, which you can show us.
- Experience interviewing customers or subject experts and turning notes into clear copy.
- Working knowledge of SEO and how to measure content against leads.
- Clear written English; you can explain a technical process without jargon.

Nice-to-haves
- Familiarity with pharma distribution, supply chain or healthcare.
- Ability to write in Hindi or Marathi.
- Experience with webinars or video scripts.

What we offer
Rs 18-26 lakh a year fixed, set by your experience. [Variable pay, if any.] [Health insurance, leave and learning budget: state the real ones.] [Growth path, as agreed with the CMO.]

About [Company]
We are a 60-person company in Pune. Our inventory software helps pharma distributors manage their stock. [Stage: profitable, funded, or other.] [Number] distributors use it today.

How to apply
Email [careers email] with the subject "Content Marketing Manager: [your name]". Attach your CV and links to 2 or 3 pieces you wrote, with one line on what each achieved. Please do not send social media pages as samples.
1. We reply to every application within 5 working days.
2. A 45-minute conversation with the CMO, held within a week of our reply.
3. A 2-hour writing task from our own customer notes, then a 30-minute discussion. We decide within 3 working days, and the whole process takes about 3 weeks.
We use your details only for this hiring process and delete them after [period] if we do not hire you. We welcome applicants of every gender, age and background.

[कथा-वाचन स्क्रिप्ट: शबरी की प्रतीक्षा, श्रीरामचरितमानस, अरण्यकांड। एक एपिसोड, लगभग 7 मिनट। नाम इसी तरह बोले जाएँ: शबरी, मतंग, पंपा, लक्ष्मण।]

जय सियाराम। प्रेम से बोलिए, सियावर रामचंद्र की जय।

सोचिए ज़रा। एक माँ, जो हर सुबह उठती है और सबसे पहले रास्ता बुहारती है। इस उम्मीद में कि शायद आज वो आ जाएँ। आज नहीं आए, तो कल। एक दिन नहीं, एक साल नहीं, बरसों तक। और जिस दिन वो सच में आए, तो उसके पास उन्हें देने के लिए क्या था? न सोना, न चाँदी। सिर्फ़ कंद, मूल और कुछ फल। आज की कथा उसी की है। शबरी की।

भक्तों, यह कथा हम गोस्वामी तुलसीदास जी के श्रीरामचरितमानस के अरण्यकांड से सुना रहे हैं। प्रसंग वहाँ का है, जब सीता जी की खोज में श्रीराम और लक्ष्मण वन-वन भटक रहे हैं। कबंध को मुक्ति देकर वे आगे बढ़ते हैं, और तुलसीदास जी लिखते हैं कि श्रीराम ने शबरी के आश्रम की ओर पग धारे। पंपा सरोवर के पास, घने वन में, यह आश्रम था।

अब वहाँ चलिए, जहाँ शबरी रहती थीं। वन की सुबह है। पीपल के पत्ते हिल रहे हैं, पंपा सरोवर का पानी ठंडा है, और मिट्टी में कंद-मूल की हल्की-सी महक है। लोक-परंपरा कहती है कि शबरी रोज़ पूरा रास्ता बुहारतीं और फल चुनकर टोकरी में रखतीं। कथावाचक यह भी बताते हैं कि गुरु मतंग मुनि ने उनसे कहा था, "बेटी, एक दिन श्रीराम तुम्हारे द्वार आएँगे।" तुलसीदास जी इतना ही कहते हैं कि शबरी ने मुनि के वचन को अपने हृदय में बैठा लिया था।

और फिर वो दिन आ गया।

तुलसीदास जी लिखते हैं कि शबरी ने जैसे ही श्रीराम को अपने घर आते देखा, उन्हें मुनि के वचन याद आ गए, और मन खिल उठा।

ज़रा सोचिए, उस पल शबरी के मन में क्या चल रहा होगा? इतने बरसों की प्रतीक्षा, और सामने वही। कमल जैसे नेत्र, लंबी भुजाएँ, सिर पर जटाओं का मुकुट, गले में वनमाला। साँवले और गोरे, दो सुंदर भाई। शबरी दौड़कर उनके चरणों से लिपट गईं। कंठ भर आया, मुँह से बोल नहीं निकले। बार-बार बस अपना सिर उनके चरण-कमलों पर रखती रहीं। आश्रम में धूप उतर आई थी, पर शबरी को न धूप का ध्यान था, न अपनी थकान का। आँखों से आँसू बह रहे थे, और होंठ बस एक ही बात कह रहे थे: आप आ गए।

फिर शबरी ने जल लिया, और बड़े आदर से दोनों भाइयों के चरण धोए। उन्हें सुंदर आसन पर बैठाया। और जो कुछ वन में था, वही सामने रख दिया। तुलसीदास जी लिखते हैं कि शबरी ने बहुत रसीले कंद, मूल और फल श्रीराम को लाकर दिए, और प्रभु ने प्रेम से, बार-बार उनकी प्रशंसा करते हुए, उन्हें खाया। ज़रा सोचिए, भक्तों। कोई राजा के सामने थाली रखे, तो उसमें सोने का मोल गिना जाता है। यहाँ थाली में सिर्फ़ जंगल था। फिर भी प्रभु बार-बार क्यों बखानते रहे? क्योंकि उन्होंने फल नहीं खाए, उन्होंने बरसों की प्रतीक्षा खाई।

कहते हैं, लोक-कथाओं में बेर वाली बात बहुत प्रसिद्ध है कि शबरी ने हर बेर चखकर मीठा चुना। यह तुलसीदास जी के मानस में नहीं लिखा, यह श्रद्धा से जुड़ी लोक-परंपरा है। पर इतना तय है कि जो प्रेम से दिया गया, श्रीराम ने वही स्वीकार किया।

अब कथा उस मोड़ पर आती है, जहाँ शबरी हाथ जोड़कर खड़ी हो जाती हैं। उन्हें अपनी कोई बड़ाई नहीं दिखती। वे श्रीराम से कहती हैं कि मैं तो अधम से भी अधम हूँ, यानी बहुत दीन-हीन, मंदबुद्धि हूँ, मैं आपकी स्तुति कैसे करूँ? सोचिए, जिसने इतनी सेवा की, वही अपने को सबसे छोटा मान रही है। और तब श्रीराम क्या कहते हैं? सुनिए:
"कह रघुपति सुनु भामिनि बाता। मानउँ एक भगति कर नाता॥"
यानी, श्रीराम कहते हैं, "भामिनि, सुनो। मैं तो सिर्फ़ एक ही रिश्ता मानता हूँ, भक्ति का रिश्ता।"

इसके आगे प्रभु समझाते हैं कि जाति, पाँति, कुल, धर्म, बड़ाई, धन, बल, परिवार और चतुराई, यह सब भक्ति के बिना ऐसे हैं, जैसे बिना जल का बादल। फिर उन्होंने शबरी को नवधा भक्ति बताई। पहली भक्ति, संतों का संग। दूसरी, मेरी कथा में प्रेम।

इसके बाद शबरी ने श्रीराम को पंपा सरोवर की ओर जाने की राह बताई, और कहा कि वहीं आपकी सुग्रीव से मित्रता होगी। जब श्रीराम चलने लगे, तो शबरी ने अपनी देह योग की अग्नि में समर्पित कर दी और हरि के चरणों में लीन हो गईं। जिसकी पूरी उम्र प्रतीक्षा थी, उसका अंत मिलन में हुआ।

अब इस कथा का भाव।
भगवान ऊँचा नाम नहीं देखते, रिश्ता देखते हैं।
इंतज़ार भी अगर प्रेम से किया जाए, तो वह पूजा बन जाता है।
और सेवा का मोल चीज़ से नहीं, भाव से तय होता है।

कल जब आप किसी की छोटी-सी भेंट को हल्का समझने लगें, तो शबरी को याद कीजिएगा। और जब कभी लगे कि आपकी प्रार्थना सुनी नहीं जा रही, तो याद रखिए, कोई है जो बरसों से रास्ता बुहार रहा था।

अगली कड़ी में पंपा सरोवर के तट पर श्रीराम की भेंट एक ब्राह्मण के वेश में आए किसी से होती है। वह कौन है, और उसने श्रीराम को कैसे पहचाना? जानने के लिए अगली कथा ज़रूर सुनिए।

बोलिए सियावर रामचंद्र की जय।
